changes.location: Clipped opening heading and its underline
changes.evidence: A single independent horizontal rule survives at the top; no recoverable sequence of letters survives above it. The illegibility is retained, and the visible rule is represented as an underline.

changes.location: Sign immediately after the clipped opening rule
changes.h: not separately given after the opening ill
changes.evidence: Only a short dark, near-vertical lower stroke remains. The upper portion is lost; a colon versus comma cannot be settled.

The lower isolated s-like spot, shallow curved joins and a last short horizontal foot are visible; the upper letter bodies are missing. Retained as an uncertain word rather than completed from the sentence.
Only a lower returning loop and a separate short right upright survive. The clipping prevents a secure choice among the three capital-A alphabets.

changes.location: End of second physical line: les and detached terminal hook
changes.evidence: The body has a tall l-shaped curve and a small lower loop; a detached dark hook sits to its right and falls slightly below the baseline. It is best taken as the terminal s, but the attached body may already contain a reduced s, leaving a possible comma. No extra comma is asserted as certain.
The capital has a broad low returning entrance, a tall narrow hooked right stem and a separate short cross-stroke; it is visibly flourished, unlike the triangular prose A in Alors below.

The first letter descends from a heavy left entry into a sharp low turn and rises on the right; no crossing bar is present. A low stop follows it. The following long hooked f and its stop meet the insertion guide. The visible first shape is read v., without replacing it by the more expected t. or r.

changes.location: First abbreviated word in the interlinear parenthesis
changes.evidence: A p descender and a shallow trailing curl are visible before ex.; distinct a and r cannot be secured. There is no independent full stop after this first abbreviation. The uncertainty p/par remains.

changes.location: Placement of parenthetical example after f.
changes.evidence: The small parenthesis stands above the main line. A long bent guide below it ends after f. and before the capital A of Alors; it is an insertion, not an underline or a new formula.

changes.location: Punctuation after the inserted closing parenthesis
changes.evidence: A high heavy head continues down into a short hooked tail after the right parenthesis, giving a comma rather than a point.

changes.location: Word broken across physical lines 5 and 6 after Alors la
changes.evidence: The line-end begins with an open c-like curve followed by on-like arches, a detached s-shaped turn and joined tru/c-like strokes. The next line begins with the reduced ion/tion ending seen in half a. The complete letter chain is not secure enough to remove the C doubt, but raisonnement does not match the initial curves. This crop covers only the end-of-line fragment; the next-line box was settled in half a and was not cropped again.

changes.location: Ending of the verb after nous
changes.evidence: After fourn, a detached dot is directly above the last low i-stroke and its short terminal tail. No following t ascender/crossbar or separate r is visible before the paper edge. The uninflected written form is retained.
A small d ascender and an initial lower oval survive under a dense multi-stroke horizontal cancellation. The second vowel cannot be distinguished as u or e. The deletion state itself is certain.

changes.location: Initial letter of the middle-term expression
changes.evidence: A heavy upright has a small top cap and a rightward upper-middle arm that turns upward at its right end. The upper bowl is not closed in this copy; P remains the first reading, with F retained.

changes.location: Right end of the middle-term expression
changes.evidence: The raised end of N is followed by a narrow blank strip and then the copying edge. There is no visible closing parenthesis on this line. The next line begins de (*) in half a, without a displaced closer.

The f, open c, crossed t, rounded o and dotted i are visible; several intervening joins and the very compressed final lité(s) group are not separable with confidence. The lexical reading is retained with the C doubt.

The inner glyph has a long top bar, a vertical descending from near its left end and a strong left hook at the foot. The ink supports T with a hooked foot but does not exclude J. H already marks the label uncertain; its doubt is preserved, not counted as a separate H error.

changes.location: Question: clipped word at the end of its first line
changes.evidence: An open low e-shaped curl survives near the right edge. Only a faint trace beyond it could belong to t; the complete word cannot be established from these strokes.

A small left curve/loop and a hooked right parenthesis enclose a dense crossing with a short upper-right spur. The central star cannot be completely separated from the surrounding curves, so its doubt remains.

changes.location: Question: space between sont and ils
changes.evidence: There is open baseline space between the terminal t of sont and the i of ils; no horizontal hyphen lies in that gap. The visible later hyphen in Connaissent-ils is a separate occurrence.
The c and o are rounded; the following n/n/u sequence is reduced to low connected turns. The final rise is too short to distinguish a terminal s from the exit of u before the right edge.

changes.location: Question: word after par les, including its accent
changes.evidence: After the first tall crossed t, the ending has low ce-like turns and a final downward s-hook, with no second t ascender; compétences rather than compétents is therefore selected for the ending. The accent above the first e is a heavy oblique wedge whose long axis leans down to the right, favouring grave è; acute é remains possible because of its thickness. The accent is not normalized from French spelling.

The end of Breen reaches the right of its line without a separate low comma stroke. The following physical line begins with the capital I of Illusie and has no initial comma. Both sides of the line break were inspected in half a.

The initial capital is densely retraced, with an open upper-right arm and a small loop near the bottom. The visible final form favours C, but the heavy stem and lower loop leave D possible. No distinct underlying letter is legible enough to add a deleted form.

After the tall crossed t is a small rise followed by a long flat exit ending in a downward hook. That compressed ending can carry es or a single e with a terminal flourish; plural grammar does not decide it.
Both ends have paired short high strokes, not angular guillemets. The opening pair is also visible in the variantes crop; the closing pair was clear in half a.
There are two short upright/slanting marks before the word and two more high strokes after it; neither pair forms an angle.
After pour the next word has a low e-shaped entry and a single low n-like wave. There is no tall l, and the following physical line clearly begins obtenir.
The initial n, short acute above the following e, open terminal c and detached low stop are individually visible in the lower half. The C doubt is removed without expanding the abbreviation.
Two light pencil digits in the outer lower-left corner are clearly 6 and 4. They are recorded as an archive comment, not as an author page number.

changes.location: Isolated raised point above the sequence label
changes.final: comment: isolated raised point; intentional status uncertain; no textual function assigned
changes.evidence: A compact dark point lies above and slightly right of the dense label. Its separation supplies no reliable attachment to an exponent or punctuation function; it may be a copying/pen speck. It is retained as an image observation rather than assigned a new mathematical exponent.

changes.location: Isolated raised point between ils and connu
changes.final: comment: isolated raised point; intentional status uncertain; no textual function assigned
changes.evidence: A second compact point is high above the blank gap after ils. It is separate from the clearly lower/left i-dot of ils and has no corresponding baseline stroke. No textual function is established.
The tall looped l runs into a closed low a-body with a short right exit. It is not the open e found elsewhere on the page.

changes.h: within the unreadable span after projectifs
changes.evidence: A small closed d-body rises into an open ascender and runs into the low e-exit before the abbreviation. This preposition is readable independently of the abbreviation.

notes: The author associates M and N respectively with K^0 and K^1 sheaves of an additive champ of projective A-Modules. The written abbreviation is read v. f.; no mathematical expansion of its first letter is assumed.

The author attributes a construction to Mme Sinh, says it gives an épinglé Picard champ, and asserts a canonical section of the middle term. P/F and the missing visible closing parenthesis are transmitted from this page; no expression is repaired from mathematical expectation.
The NB claims the preceding material has evident functorialities in M,N,X. This is an author assertion, not a verification by this reader.

The final block asks whether the triangle and exact sequence are known to the named people Quillen, Breen and Illusie, then asks about higher variants. The parenthetical suggestion uses pourrait and proposes a geometric principle through n-champs de Picard non néc. stricts; it is not presented here as a proved result.

The degree glyphs K^0/K^1, ring alphabet, P/F and two references to (*) prompted ink inspection. No targeted proof, counterexample search, derivation, or external mathematical comparison was performed; checks is therefore empty.

The copied first line is clipped above its lower fragments. No author page number or date is visible. H page{6} is treated as its page locator, not imported as manuscript ink. Archive foliation 64 is present in pencil and is recorded only as a comment.
The two curved marks at the lower left of the internal frame are copying impressions, not a drawing or a marginal note. They are described in a comment and not counted as words omitted by H.

Two isolated points above the Question text were inspected in the already required crops. Their intentional status remains uncertain and no mathematical or punctuation function can be assigned; comments and per-locus records preserve the observations without inventing an exponent.

The accent in compètences is retained as a grave-first uncertainty because the visible wedge slopes down right. The ending ce(s), rather than a second t, is clearer. Neither normal French spelling nor the H editorial note was used to settle the mark.

coverage: Read the one whole image once for layout, then each supplied half once in order, against every C and H word and mathematical sign, including their agreements. All 21 physical text lines, the clipped heading, both underlined paragraph leads, every inline formula and degree, both parenthetical references, the interlinear example and its guide, the definite cancellation, quotation strokes, accents, endings, punctuation, page edges and all margins were inspected. Fourteen tight crops were made only for places left unresolved; each was viewed once, with no repeat whole/half view or repeat crop. The split construction locus and the possible punctuation after Breen have explicit boxes on both physical lines; crop 05 covers only the construction line end, and the other side was read in half a. There are no independent displays, diagrams, author drawings or marginal notes. H omits the cancellation and insertion state, supplies a closing parenthesis and two punctuation/hyphen marks not visible, and has a different article/noun pair and a different en/les reading. C doubts were either explicitly retained or resolved in changes. The terminal mark at les and the accent of compètences receive new uncertainty; two otherwise unassigned raised points are preserved in comments and structured records. Archive 64 and copying impressions are accounted for.
